cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: For the Record
cards.instruction: Get someone to state exactly what they did, knew, or authorized before you reveal your own involvement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before I show you my dinner invitations, who did you authorize your sister to bring?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A date. Did you invite my ex?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Did you name anyone she couldn't bring? Then we'll get to my list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. My ex. I sent you both the same message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What time did you send it to me? I'll put that beside my invitation's timestamp before we open it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 withholds invitation list, A3 controls B2 question timing, A5 demands message time before opening A invitation; assumed jurisdiction shapes the staged record disclosure.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 date permission and ex suspicion cause A3 exclusions question; B4 explicit exclusion sent to both causes A5 received-time inquiry.

relationship.evidence: B2 asks about a personally important invitee and B4 gives concrete evidence of notice, not just a stock accusation.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 message to compare timestamps before disclosure, tightening the account demanded from B.

specificity.evidence: A1 dinner invitations and sister guest, B4 shared exclusion message establish roles and stakes without knowing the hidden list.
